Previous statement: Every non-constant polynomial has a root in the complex numbers.
Revised statement: Every nonconstant polynomial with complex coefficients has a root in $\mathbb C$.

Previous statement: The numbers of positive, negative and zero eigenvalues of a symmetric matrix don't depend on the choice of basis.
Revised statement: For a real symmetric matrix $A$ and any invertible real matrix $P$, the matrices $A$ and $P^TAP$ have the same numbers of positive, negative and zero eigenvalues.
Reason: Inertia is invariant under congruence of quadratic forms, not a vague change of matrix basis.

Previous statement: A double integral of an integrable function can be computed as an iterated integral in either order.
Revised statement: If $f$ is continuous on $[a,b]\times[c,d]$, then $\displaystyle\int_a^b\!\int_c^d f(x,y)\,dy\,dx=\int_c^d\!\int_a^b f(x,y)\,dx\,dy=\iint_{[a,b]\times[c,d]}f$.
Reason: State a precise course-appropriate case with all hypotheses, and distinguish its formulation from the dated general theorem.
